thread.title: Power Integrations' Revenue Re-Acceleration Looking More Like A 2019 Event - Power Integrations, Inc. (NASDAQ:POWI)

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: Power Integrations' Revenue Re-Acceleration Looking More Like A 2019 Event - Power Integrations, Inc. (NASDAQ:POWI)
text:
All you need to be a successful semiconductor loved by investors is perpetual double-digit revenue growth, 60%-plus gross margins, 30%-plus operating margins, a rich buyback, expanding end-markets, and optionality on both ends of the M&A spectrum. See? Simple.
Sarcasm aside, Power Integrations ( POWI ) has been in a tougher spot recently, with the company missing a few times on the top line and lowering guidance. A slowdown in smartphones and communications and delays in other programs has pushed revenue growth down from the double-digits, and the margins remain sub-optimal. Add in a relatively robust valuation, and I’m not too surprised that the shares have lagged the SOX by a significant degree since my last update , not to mention underperforming peers/rivals like ON Semiconductor ( ON ). With the shares already pricing in a return to double-digit revenue and a mid-20%’s operating margin, it’s tough for me to see a compelling risk-adjusted opportunity here.
Handsets Waiting On Rapid Charging, Chinese Volume, And Apple Between weaker smartphone volumes and ongoing weakness in China’s telecom deployments, Power Integrations had a pretty rough first quarter in its communications business, with a one-third year-over-year drop in revenue. The good news, though, is that Chinese handset volumes have picked up since then, and Power Integrations should see improving volume through its relationship with Huawei .
Beyond this, I see two major drivers for potentially higher smartphone-driven revenue. First is the ongoing adoption of rapid charging. With its InnoSwitch technology, Power Integrations offers a simpler solution for OEMs (roughly one-third the number of components), but also one that earns the company about 2x-3x the content value. Rapid charging adoption was running around one-third at the start of this year, but has continued to expand since then, creating a larger addressable market for POWI.
The second potential driver is to win business away from companies like Dialog ( OTCPK:DLGNF ) and ON with smartphone OEMs. Dialog has held the majority of the early rapid charging market and companies like ON and NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) have been tough competitors in the broader phone power adapter space. There were rumors and hopes of POWI gaining business with Apple ( AAPL ) for the iPhone 8/X cycle which proved unfounded, but the prospect of winning more OEMs over to their solutions remains a potential driver for POWI.
Longer-Term Opportunities In Bigger Applications Although high-power applications are a small part of Power Integrations’ mix today (around 10%), I expect this to grow in time as the company leverages its SCALE and SCALE-2 platforms in applications above 100kW. These platforms are relevant to applications like motor drives, medical equipment, and solar inverters, as well as EV drivetrains and EV charging stations, not to mention industrial electrification and DC transmission.
Part of my bullish thesis on ABB ( ABB ) is predicated on ongoing growth in industrial/factory automation, and such automation is going to require substantial industrial electrification. Likewise, transmission grids around the world need to be upgraded and expanded to improve reliability and include renewable sources. Last and not least, if predictions that EVs could make up one-quarter of passenger vehicle sales in 2030 have any chance of being accurate, there are going to have to be significant investments in charging stations throughout the U.S., Europe, and China. All of these are opportunities for ABB, but also for Power Integrations’ high-power business.
Waiting For The Return To Double-Digit Growth There were hopes that 2018 would see Power Integrations return to double-digit growth, but after first quarter results and guidance, that no longer seems like a likely outcome. Even so, the company has good leverage to rapid charging and UBS-PD adoption. With USB-PD allowing up to 100W of power delivery, and the company’s partnership with Cypress ( CY ) (which supplies the USB-C port controller), this could be a meaningful driver for the company from the second half of 2018 on, with adoption in a variety of consumer devices (including computers, phones, and other rechargeable consumer electronics).
The Opportunity The next twelve months should see Power Integrations looking at a healthier smartphone market, with increased rapid charging and USB-PD adoption, a healthier wireline market, and ongoing industrial growth from drivers like automation, IoT, lighting, and power transmission. I believe that will restore double-digit growth for at least a brief window of time.
I expect above-trend growth for Power Integrations in 2019-2022, with a long-term revenue growth trend of around 5% to 6%. I also expect ongoing progress with margins, though I’m skeptical about POWI ever reaching the 60/30 promised land.
The Bottom Line Power Integrations doesn’t look cheap on a DCF or margin-drive EV/revenue basis, with the current price already anticipating a meaningful step up in both revenue growth and margins. While I’m bullish on opportunities like rapid charging/USB-PD and increased adoption of POWI solutions by industrial customers, I think that’s already in the price. All told, I’m not inclined to overpay for these shares, and particularly when the company is still not on a great trajectory of beating and raising expectations.
Disclosure: I am/we are long ABB.
